evidence.notes: Kaplan et al. 2012: Figure 2A/D, Results and Discussion, Tables S1/S2 and Text S1. Native figures and rendered supplements inspected. Viability in Table S1 is not an independent drug-resistance endpoint; growth and purified-enzyme contexts remain distinct.

Reference-only RPO21/RPB1, YDL140C, SGD:S000002299; UniProt release 2026_03, entry version 255, sequence version 2, retrieved 2026-10-14. S288c reference taxon 559292 belongs to species 4932 in cached UniProt Taxonomy. These are not tested derivative or mutant-specific accessions.

claims.label: RPB1-associated laboratory mycophenolic-acid resistance (qualified association)
claims.note: Selected RPB1 laboratory comparisons are labeled resistant in Figure 2D; Figure 2A provides matched growth controls. Other RPB1 comparisons are sensitive or have baseline growth defects. This is not a shared effect of all RPB1 alleles, a clinical resistance category, an MIC, or a species-wide phenotype. Text S1 identifies S288C-derived backgrounds and CKY283 as the genetic-comparison parent, not as an identifier for every tested derivative. RPB1 is the paper's name for RPO21. UniProtKB:P04050 and NCBITaxon:559292 identify S288c reference context only; no exact experimental protein, allele, strain TaxID or genome is assigned. The accompanying IMD transcription results do not make Rpb1 a direct drug target; the Figure 5A probe is not uniquely IMD2-specific.
claims.phenotype_label: Source-defined laboratory resistance to mycophenolic acid
